experiment_template.research_question: Does H21 preserve multiple independent facts while history fits, and lose them under actual token-admission pressure?
stop_conditions: No live provider calls before separately frozen execution binding.
No retry or trial replacement; preserve source, receipt and cleanup failures.
No serving changes or modifications of frozen H21.

success_criteria.construction: Co-located controls retain both original facts; H21 split unpressured cases retain both; independent sandbox checks agree.
success_criteria.interpretation: Byte blocks, missing exposure, failed controls and unavailable calibration are inconclusive, not semantic counterevidence.
success_criteria.pressure: Demonstrate full-history rejection and reduced-history admission with actual tokenizer counts and prior decisive read delivery before interpreting correctness.

falsifier: Unpressured controls fail, or exact older source evidence and correct joint semantics survive actual measured fallback pressure.
mechanism: Full-history admission preserves all observed bodies; a fallback keeping only the newest exchange removes earlier independent sources. The prior synthetic tool-count pressure does not establish the real capacity boundary.
scope: Diagnostic construction and measured-token feasibility first; no claim of live model quality or a new retention policy from scripted responders.
statement: H21 preserves independently revised facts while complete history fits, but its one-exchange fallback loses older facts when actual token admission forces recycling.
